purpose: Compact reusable source-understanding knowledge distilled from synthetic OCL/FDD training engagements. This is supporting evidence only; current source evidence always wins.
core_principles: Never infer a field's meaning from its heading alone. Use sample values, neighboring fields, sheet/workbook context, cardinality, formatting, hierarchy, related datasets and current-source evidence.
A worksheet can contain zero, one or multiple logical datasets. Blank separator rows, different headers, changed column layouts and changed grains are strong dataset-boundary evidence.
Report titles, preambles, commentary, subtotal rows, grand totals, formula rows and presentation-only sections are not underlying transactional records unless current evidence proves otherwise.
Merged cells, hidden rows/columns, indentation and formatting are structural evidence, not data by themselves.
Do not assume every balance inside Current Liabilities is OCL. Economic substance matters more than words such as accrual, payable, creditor, liability or provision.
Prior reusable knowledge is evidence only. If the current dataset contradicts prior knowledge, the current dataset wins.
Incomplete mappings must remain visible and traceable. Never drop an unmapped record merely because a mapping field is blank.
Actual, Budget and Variance sections must be distinguished. Do not treat management-calculated KPIs or variance columns as source accounting balances without evidence.
A large, volatile, new, stable or year-end-elevated accrual is not automatically an issue. Require corroborating accounting or operational evidence before drawing an FDD conclusion.
Where evidence is insufficient for an analysis, mark it unsupported or partial rather than manufacturing a conclusion.

patterns.guidance: Finance workbooks commonly have title/preamble rows followed by blank rows before the real header. Preserve preamble as context and identify the primary header from the tabular region rather than assuming row 1.

A single sheet may contain independent GL/account-level and site/location-level datasets with different grains and partially different columns. Split them when structure/grain changes rather than forcing one schema.

Wide monthly management reports may contain Actual/Budget/Variance sections, merged quarter headers and separator columns. Identify the actual accounting section and normalize periods without treating quarter headers/separators as records.

Annual balance-sheet summaries often have years horizontally with parent/child hierarchy, indentation and subtotal/formula rows. Reconstruct leaf/detail balances separately from presentation totals and preserve hierarchy.
The same conceptual dataset may arrive in long format, wide monthly format or separate entity sheets across years/files. Determine conceptual equivalence from grain and fields, not layout identity.

Names such as Cat, Map1, Description, Mapping, Class, Amount and Cost Code are intentionally ambiguous in real client files. Infer semantics contextually; the same heading can mean different things in different datasets.

Mapping schedules are supporting evidence for account/category relationships. Expect partial mappings and preserve unmatched accounts for explicit review rather than silently assigning or excluding them.

Payroll/bonus/employee schedules can support accrual reasonableness, seasonality and settlement. Different payroll sheets can have different grains (employee, department, month) and should not be forced into one raw layout.

Detailed project accrual schedules can support roll-forward analysis. Where definitions align, test Opening + Additions - Utilisation - Release +/- Reclass +/- FX = Closing. Never plug an unexplained difference.

Subsequent invoices/payments can evidence settlement, utilization and potential completeness, but a post-close invoice does not automatically mean a missing accrual. Link to the underlying obligation and closing accrual first.

Contract/milestone/certified-work evidence can support adequacy/completeness for selected accruals. It supports an evidence-based concern or reconciliation; do not automatically quantify an adjustment without full support.
Monthly P&L/expense data can support accrual-to-expense and QoE analysis. Preserve the expense category/period/entity/project dimensions needed to link balances to expense activity.
True aging requires actual accrual/obligation dates. Repeated unchanged monthly balances are only a stale-balance proxy and must not be described as true age without date evidence.

Potential duplicates require multiple corroborating identifiers such as vendor, project, PO/contract and service period. Similar descriptions alone are insufficient; similar-looking records may represent different obligations.

Nearby liability accounts are investigation candidates, not automatic OCL. Separate normal operating accruals from trade payables, tax, financing, lease, deferred-income/customer-funding and potential debt-like/capex items using economic substance and transaction context.
Seasonality, invoice timing and recurring settlement cycles can make balances large or volatile without indicating an issue. Compare multi-period history and supporting activity before escalating.
A balance appearing for the first time may reflect genuine business expansion or project mobilisation. Establish expected recurrence and operational support before calling it one-off or abnormal.
A material balance remaining unchanged for several months can be a stale-balance indicator. Stronger conclusions require obligation dates, utilization, invoices/payments or management support.

A sharp Oct-Dec build followed by Jan-Feb unwind may be seasonal, settlement timing or estimation behavior. Compare historical recurrence and post-close evidence before concluding on normalized working capital.

Total OCL can remain stable while composition changes materially. Analyse category/project/employee shares because mix shift may affect closing representativeness and normalized NWC even without a large total movement.
Separate genuine FX translation/revaluation from underlying operational movement where currency evidence exists. Do not describe all reported movement as business growth or release.

Balances against closed sites/completed projects warrant validity and transaction-treatment review, but some may remain valid and settle normally. Investigate rather than automatically excluding them from NWC.

Evidence requirements: seasonality/volatility need monthly balances; utilization/releases need movement data; accrual-to-expense needs P&L; true aging needs dates; adequacy/completeness need obligation/contract/AP/subsequent-payment evidence; duplicate testing needs record-level identifiers. Mark unsupported tests explicitly.

Partner output should connect factual analysis to normalized NWC, net debt/equity value, QoE, completeness, closing representativeness, settlement or adequacy. State evidence limitations and ask targeted factual questions; do not turn an indicator into an unsupported adjustment.
